newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Ukraine minister denies Chernobyl radiation rise.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine minister denies Chernobyl radiation rise.

text.p: No increases in radiation or temperature were registered at the Chernobyl nuclear plant earlier this week, a Ukrainian minister said on Wednesday.

"No radiation or temperature changes were registered," Yuri Kostenko, Ukraine's minister for nuclear safety, told Reuters during a conference in Vienna, contradicting remarks made by Chernobyl officials on Tuesday.
"There was an increase in neutron activity. If this were a nuclear reaction it would have to be accompanied by a rise in temperature and radiation, but these factors were not measured," he said.

Officials at the station said on Tuesday there had been sharp increases in neutron activity and temperature inside the "sarcophagus", the protective casing erected after Chernobyl's fourth reactor exploded on April 26, 1986, sending a radioactive cloud over much of Europe.
Kostenko said his ministry had formed a "special group" to look into the incident, adding that the registered increase in neutron activity might be due to faulty measuring equipment.

"We need to review our investigations inside the sarcophagus but we have no money. We are now in contact with the U.S. government," said the minister, who was attending the International Atomic Energy Agency's annual congress in Vienna.
